limitations: The exact transaction is canonical and the negotiation path is preserved in stored contemporary negotiation history.

Robert explicitly remembers Jeremiyah Love as the primary target for Rookie 1.02 and Tetairoa McMillan as the desired FA 1.01 target; both are also supported by later-documented 2026 draft decision context.

Aaron Jones was viewed as highly movable because of age, salary and recent injury/role concerns. Exact additional value Robert would have paid beyond Jones is not numerically reconstructed, only that the executed price was comfortably below his ceiling.
Later 2026 outcomes for Love, McMillan, Jones and the moved draft positions are excluded from the original trade judgment.

evidence_basis.note: Confirms Robert received Rookie 1.02 and FA 1.01 and sent Aaron Jones, Rookie 1.03 and FA 1.04.

Contemporary history shows Robert wanted to move from Rookie 1.03 to Dennis's 1.02, simplified the negotiation after Dennis found the initial long message overwhelming, and ultimately paired the Rookie move-up with an FA 1.04-to-1.01 move and Aaron Jones. Dennis accepted the cleaner construction.

Later-preserved draft decision context identifies Jeremiyah Love as Robert's premium Rookie 1.02 selection and class-best RB target. This supports the reconstructed target identity while later player outcomes remain excluded.

Robert explicitly remembers Jeremiyah Love as the clear primary target for Rookie 1.02 and Tetairoa McMillan as the desired FA 1.01 target. Love was the main reason for the trade; McMillan and FA 1.01 were an additional high-value bonus rather than the core requirement.

Robert remembers Aaron Jones as highly movable trade material because of age, relatively high salary, prior-season injuries and Jordan Mason's involvement. The executed price felt very cheap / no-brainer. Robert would likely have paid more if needed. Final calibration: Decision Confidence 5/5; Outcome Uncertainty no more than 2/5.

decision_context.objective: Secure Jeremiyah Love by moving from Rookie 1.03 to 1.02, while also upgrading FA 1.04 to FA 1.01 to secure Tetairoa McMillan, using Aaron Jones as expendable veteran bridge value.
decision_context.roster_context: Aaron Jones was not a core long-term piece for Robert. His age, injury history, salary and role pressure from Jordan Mason made him highly movable. Robert was willing to convert that veteran value into premium draft-position certainty.
decision_context.cap_salary_context: Jones's relatively high salary increased his expendability and strengthened the logic of moving him for younger premium assets.
decision_context.team_window: Robert was a contender but still prioritized premium young assets with long-term ceiling, especially a top young RB prospect in Love.
decision_context.market_context: Robert had already failed to acquire Tim's 1.01, but Tim had indicated a target path that left Robert believing Love could be secured at 1.02. FA 1.01 also offered the most attractive free-agent prospect on Robert's board, Tetairoa McMillan.
decision_context.why_now: Dennis controlled exactly the Rookie slot Robert needed and the top FA slot. The deal allowed Robert to lock in both target positions before either market could move.
constraints: Rookie 1.02 was the primary objective because Robert wanted Jeremiyah Love.
FA 1.01 and Tetairoa McMillan were valuable additional upside but not the deciding reason to make the deal.
Aaron Jones was viewed as intentionally movable rather than protected.
Robert would likely have paid more than the executed package if necessary, but the exact hard ceiling is not reconstructed.

theses.statement: Moving from Rookie 1.03 to 1.02 was worth meaningful veteran value because it converted board uncertainty into control over Jeremiyah Love, Robert's clear premium RB target.
falsification_conditions: Love was not materially preferred to the likely 1.03 alternatives on Robert's ex-ante board.
The probability of Love being available at 1.03 was high enough that paying to move up created unnecessary cost.

theses.statement: Upgrading FA 1.04 to FA 1.01 added major value because Robert already viewed Tetairoa McMillan as the best available FA-market prospect.
falsification_conditions: McMillan was not materially stronger than the realistic FA 1.04 shelf.
Robert's expected FA board did not justify paying for first-choice control.

theses.statement: Aaron Jones was efficient outgoing currency because his age, salary, injury history and role uncertainty made him more replaceable than the premium young assets the move-ups could secure.
falsification_conditions: Jones remained materially more important to Robert's contender lineup than reconstructed.
Jones's market value could have bought substantially more without risking the target slots.

alternatives.description: Stay at Rookie 1.03 and accept whichever premium player remained.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert specifically wanted Jeremiyah Love and preferred certainty over accepting a fallback.

alternatives.description: Acquire Rookie 1.02 without the FA move-up.
alternatives.reason_not_chosen: Robert says he would still have liked the Rookie move on its own, but Dennis's accepted construction also delivered FA 1.01 at an attractive total price.
Jones was intentionally movable because of age, salary, injury history and role concerns.

price_ceiling.description: The executed package was comfortably below Robert's acceptable maximum. Robert remembers he would have added more if necessary to secure the combination, especially Rookie 1.02, but no exact hard maximum is reconstructed.

known_risks.description: Love and McMillan were still young/prospect assets, so there remained some normal developmental uncertainty despite Robert's strong conviction.
Paying to move only one Rookie slot could have been unnecessary if Love would have survived to 1.03.
Moving Jones reduced proven veteran RB depth for a contender.

decision_state_at_execution.confidence_rationale: Robert remembers the trade as a very cheap no-brainer. Love was the clear primary target, McMillan was an additional premium target, and Jones was deliberately movable veteran value rather than a painful outgoing asset.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_confidence_driver: Control of the exact premium Rookie and FA targets at a price centered on an older, higher-salary, replaceable RB.
decision_state_at_execution.primary_source_of_doubt: Only normal prospect development uncertainty remained; Robert did not meaningfully doubt the transaction itself.
known_personal_biases: Strong target conviction toward Jeremiyah Love.
Strong target conviction toward Tetairoa McMillan.

portfolio_links.description: Like the preceding Pickens consolidation, this move converted expendable veteran/depth value into more concentrated premium young-asset control.
